title: ClosureX: Compiler Support for Correct Persistent Fuzzing
problem: Persistent fuzzing reuses a single process across multiple test cases to eliminate process creation/teardown overhead, but process state changes from one test case (heap state, file descriptors, global variables, etc.) persist into subsequent test cases, causing semantic inconsistencies that lead to missed crashes, false crashes, and overall incorrectness in fuzzer-discovered bugs.
motivation: Persistent fuzzing provides the highest fuzzing throughput by reusing processes, and since bug discovery rate scales directly with throughput, fixing semantic inconsistency is essential to realizing persistent fuzzing's performance advantage without sacrificing correctness.
method: ClosureX is a compiler tool that identifies which parts of your program's state (memory, file handles, global variables) change during each test case and determines the minimal set that must be reset between tests. The tool automatically inserts code into the fuzzing loop to save a snapshot of this state before each test and restore it afterward. This approach lets you run many tests in one process (persistent fuzzing) while preventing one test's leftover state from affecting the next, without needing to restart the entire process.
key_novelty: A compiler that automatically identifies the minimal program state requiring reset between fuzzing iterations, enabling correct persistent fuzzing without process recreation overhead.
contributions: Formalization of the semantic inconsistency problem in persistent fuzzing and characterization of state-pollution sources.
ClosureX compiler pass for automatic closure analysis identifying the minimal state requiring per-iteration restoration.
Instrumentation of the persistent fuzzing loop-back path for efficient state snapshot and restore.
Evaluation demonstrating both correctness restoration (eliminating false/missed crashes) and throughput maintenance.
limitations: Specific runtime overhead of closure snapshot/restore and completeness of static analysis for complex heap patterns not available from abstract.
primary_theme: compiler-based closure analysis for correct persistent fuzzing
